words.definition: existing in large quantities; plentiful
words.example: The garden had an abundant harvest of tomatoes.

words.definition: quick and energetic
words.example: They took a brisk walk before dinner.

words.definition: careful to avoid danger or mistakes
words.example: He was cautious crossing the icy road.

words.definition: to amaze or blind with bright light
words.example: The fireworks dazzled the crowd.

words.definition: very excited and wanting to do something
words.example: She was eager to open her presents.

words.definition: easily broken or damaged
words.example: Handle the glass vase, it's fragile.

words.definition: extremely large
words.example: A gigantic wave crashed on the shore.

words.definition: to pause before doing something
words.example: Don't hesitate to ask for help.

words.definition: extremely large or great
words.example: The immense mountain towered above them.

words.definition: feeling great joy; triumphant
words.example: The team was jubilant after winning.

words.definition: sharp or very interested
words.example: She has a keen sense of smell.

words.definition: giving off light; glowing
words.example: The luminous stars filled the night sky.

words.definition: to copy the way someone acts or speaks
words.example: The parrot can mimic human speech.

words.definition: quick and light in movement
words.example: The nimble cat leapt onto the fence.

words.definition: something that blocks your way
words.example: They cleared every obstacle on the course.

words.definition: strange or unusual
words.example: There was a peculiar smell in the room.

words.definition: to shake slightly, often from cold, fear, or excitement
words.example: Her hands began to tremble when she opened the mysterious box.

words.definition: very bright, clear, and easy to picture in your mind
words.example: She painted a vivid sunset full of orange and pink.

words.definition: to make something dirty or unsafe by adding germs or harmful stuff
words.example: Dirty hands can contaminate the food you're about to eat.

words.definition: a person who leads part of a government, or a person who leads religious services
words.example: The minister of education announced a new plan for schools.

words.definition: a piece so tiny you almost can't see it — like the smallest bit of something
words.example: A speck of dust is a tiny particle floating in the air.

words.definition: having to do with breaking down food so your body can use it
words.example: Your stomach is part of your digestive system.

words.definition: to press and fold dough with your hands over and over
words.example: She kneaded the bread dough until it was smooth.

words.definition: following rules very carefully and expecting others to do the same
words.example: Our coach is strict about arriving on time for practice.

words.definition: pulled something suddenly and with force
words.example: He yanked the door open when he heard the alarm.

words.definition: a heavy object dropped from a boat to hold it in place; also, to hold something firmly down
words.example: The ship dropped its anchor so it wouldn't drift away.

words.definition: a tube with a plunger and needle used to give medicine or take blood
words.example: The nurse filled the syringe before giving him his shot.

words.definition: someone who takes things from others without giving anything back
words.example: He was a freeloader who never chipped in for snacks.

words.definition: almost exactly, but not quite — about that much
words.example: The trip takes approximately two hours.

words.definition: to grab something quickly and firmly
words.example: She seized the rope before it slipped away.

words.definition: extremely bad or terrible
words.example: The weather was atrocious, so the game was cancelled.

words.definition: how well your mind and feelings are doing, just like physical health is about your body
words.example: Talking about your worries is good for your mental health.

words.definition: to seem to escape the pull that keeps things on the ground
words.example: The gymnast seemed to defy gravity as she flipped through the air.

words.definition: an injury to the brain from a hard bump or hit to the head
words.example: He wore a helmet to help prevent a concussion.

words.definition: what is meant to happen to someone in the future
words.example: She felt it was her destiny to become a scientist.

words.definition: to move something carefully and skillfully, often into a tight spot
words.example: He had to maneuver the cart around the narrow corner.
